title: Strict extension adjoint to coefficient-level evaluation
statement: Let J be an essentially small site, O a commutative ring and ell an element, and put B_n=(O/(ell^(n+1)))_J for n in N [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. In the category of strict successive semilinear systems of B_n-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], iterated transitions satisfy the identity, successor and composition equations. There are additive extension functors E_n left adjoint to evaluation e_n, with E_n F evaluated at q isomorphic to F tensor over B_n with B_q for q<=n and zero for n<q [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Choose the ordinary scalar adjunction by its value on 1 tensor x. For every map f:E_n F to M, its qth component, transported by the below-level isomorphism and transposed by that scalar adjunction, equals the n-level adjunct of f followed by the iterated transition of M. No completeness, regularity, cartesianness or normalization of the systems is assumed.

source.place: Construction 4.1, printed p. 21: the functors e_n! and (Le_n!, e_n^-1), with indices shifted from n >= 0 to n >= 1. The natural sigma maps are the truncation inclusions in its explicit formula; the Hom identity specifies their adjunction mates.

proof.text: Form the actual quotient ring diagram and the equivalence between successor systems and all-transition strict ring systems. Use the general single-level extension adjunction and its below/above formulas. The equivalence has identity components on levels and morphisms.

The general scalar model has exactly the prescribed tensor objects and maps, so the scalar functors are equal. Both normalized scalar adjunctions evaluate on the sheafification image of 1 tensor x; hence their Hom equivalences agree. Transport the general single-level Hom formula through these equalities. Additivity follows from the adjunction.
